transcript: ooooh hello this is the audience mask from Life & Trust the new show from the American producers of Sleep No More I saw it this week so I'm gonna do a whole low-down on what to expect, what I thought, and I'm gonna try to tackle the big question everyone's asking which is: is it worth the money? first thing I wanna clarify though just cause I've seen some confused about this online is that this is not from the same creators, the same artists as Sleep No More. sleep no more was created by a British company called Punchdrunk but when it came to the US this other company, Emursive produced and ran the commercial production and they're the ones who created Life & Trust so any similarities to sleep no more here are, effectively, imitation whether that imitation is effective or not, I'll get to but I just wanted to establish that bit of context first to avoid confusion so just to set the scene a bit here Life & Trust is a spin on the Faust story of someone selling their soul to the devil here it's paralleled with themes of capitalism the Wall Street Crash it's actually performed inside an old bank. (as a side note it's actually the bank from Inside Man in case anyone else is a fan of that movie) and the experience of the show is very much like sleep no more you explore these elaborately designed spaces across multiple floors you can follow the actors it's told largely through movement and dance so for better or for worse the format of the show is nearly identical. I think there are only two loops though, instead of three that's what I heard although I didn't really have my bearings enough to confirm that personally but I did have a later entry time of 8pm and the show ended at about 10:30 as far as the scale of the show it seemed very similar to me as Sleep No more like I was still stumbling across new rooms right up until the end of the show even though I thought I had explored it pretty thoroughly. A couple of aesthetic or qualitative differences that I'd point out: first of all both shows have a mix of like more literal rooms and rooms that feel more like art installation I'd say Life & Trust leans a bit more literal but it's actually just as impressive in a different way my friend described it as like being on a movie set also I think I liked the dance in this show a bit more it was done by the Kuperman brothers who did The Outsiders, so if you think about the rumble scene that they did on the Tonys there is stuff like that in this show and it's very exciting I should mention that I'm coming from a place where I love sleep no more, I admire it I've been three times but I'm also critical of it from a story standpoint and so I'm facing a similar dilemma that I did with Burnt City which was the most recent show that Punchdrunk did in London where like people were complaining that it was difficult to follow what was happening and I was like “yes…you're not wrong, but I would also say the same thing about sleep no more” I guess I can follow Sleep no more a little better just cause I know Macbeth but like, coherent storytelling is not what I get out of that show and I would say the same thing here okay, so now as far as the big question of whether it's worth the $160 price tag I'll try to answer but it's a little tricky first of all I have to disclose I was not invited by the production to see it but I did see it for free it was kind of a random thing of I was the plus one of someone who knew someone who knew someone but it was just lucky. so like, obviously that's important take it with a grain of salt but I still think I can provide some perspective because like I paid for sleep no more, I paid for Burnt City I paid for Then She Fell so, I have a personal metric of what I think these types of performances are worth to me and I was keeping that in mind as I watched it obviously this depends on your financial situation if you're fortunate enough that $160 doesn't mean that much to you then yes I would say this show is worth your time But let's say you're a little more like me: I am obviously also fortunate that I have some disposable income and I can see a lot of theater but I can't go around spending $160 on a single theater ticket willy nilly like that would be in the top five most expensive theater tickets I've ever purchased in my life and I'll be honest and say that before I lucked into this opportunity I was planning to wait for discounts maybe I would pay full price down the line if I saved up and if there was enough hype but I was not in a hurry to spend $160 so pending your financial situation here is the advice that I would give: if you're the type of person who actively seeks out these experiences especially multiple times just because you like being in that state, you like stimulating that feeling of exploration and discovery and feeling transported then yesx I would recommend it cause like, the production is very cool and these are new characters and new spaces and rooms for you to explore you do get that But, if you're the type of person who went to sleep no more once or twice because everyone said you should and it was this iconic thing and maybe you even loved it because of how unusual it was and you never knew anything could be like that but then you never really felt much of a need to go back then I wouldn't necessarily say that you need to go see this show especially if you're worried about the price tag so that would be my advice obviously take it with a grain of salt use your own judgment but I hope it helps
